title: I built a system that can one-shot full 3D games in the Unity Engine
author: Feisty-Carrot-3076
selftext:
You can play the games right now at [GameSlop.ai](http://GameSlop.ai) ! There's 5 games so far and I'll be adding more regularly (no monetization or signup required; all games playable in web but not mobile). The games span multiple genres including platformers, incremental, and even a deckbuilder.

The coolest part is that these games are actually made in the Unity game engine, so they can serve as prototypes to quickly test ideas and then directly springboard full production.

I'll be opening it up for submissions soon so anyone can pitch their idea for generation, so please sign up for the newsletter if you're interested (or just want to play more slop)!

comments.author: test_user23
comments.body: Oof. Well atleast your url is true to its name..

replies.author: Feisty-Carrot-3076
replies.body: yup lol. they dont look pretty but it is generated from a single prompt!

replies.author: test_user23
replies.body: People need to get past the one shot mindset. There’s nothing great or boastful about it.

replies.author: Feisty-Carrot-3076
replies.body: very unique take but i disagree. the ability to one-shot something generally means that subsequent shots will only be more powerful, which is why its a widely used benchmark across AI research

replies.author: test_user23
replies.body:
It’s not a unique take. Anyone who actually works with AI beyond the surface or the general public all share the same mindset.   
That just shows your lack of understanding of when it comes to AI. It’s not trying to create something good, unique, detailed, or optimized. it’s just trying to achieve the goal as quickly as possible, which is why your URL including the word SLOP is so fitting here.

replies.author: Feisty-Carrot-3076
replies.body: well I’m glad you got the joke at least!

replies.author: teamharder
replies.body: One shots only prove so much though. They do nothing to really expose the current weak spots of models. Notice how your games have no UI and are built out of basic shapes? We need to build better if we're to overcome the bias people have against AI. We need to get systems in place that can rival AA and AAA games for a fraction of the time and budget. I appreciate the enthusiasm, I really do, but stuff like this only hurts the image of AI.

replies.author: Feisty-Carrot-3076
replies.body:
this system is a multi-agent harness running through the Unity MCP. the fact that it can build games inside of the Unity engine in one-shot is actually an *accidental byproduct* of a Unity AI gamedev workflow.

i am not trying to make a statement or to be a freedom fighter for the fight against antis lol. that's not my mission. maybe showing the one-shots is distorting whats really going on under the hood, but what i'm showing here is a harness that is fully integrated with the Unity game engine to build features and games, which is something that Unity's own integrated AI can barely do.

replies.author: teamharder
replies.body:
So far as I can tell, most of the Unity MCP skills on Github are capable of similar results. There's 2-3 different ones.

What is special about your workflow? Im working on a router centered around Unity, so Im curious.

replies.author: Feisty-Carrot-3076
replies.body: A Unity MCP skill is just a tool to allow agents to interface directly with Unity instead of binary file edits or editor scripts. It's just one component of a system like this. I'm not aware of any GitHub repos that can achieve similar results to this--could you please share them?

replies.author: Feisty-Carrot-3076
replies.body: That’s just MCP interface tooling. There’s nothing in there that actually tells it how to make a game or actual game mechanics.

replies.author: teamharder
replies.body: Ah got it. Well good luck developing the workflow.

replies.author: theflossboss1
replies.body: Not a unique take at all, most of these “1 shot” builds can just be downloaded for free as a packaged system either on the unity game store or some high schooler’s GitHub.  At least then there is documentation that goes beyond the usual Claude junk

replies.author: Feisty-Carrot-3076
replies.body: I’m not aware of any agent system currently that can 1 shot a game in Unity (even if poorly). Can you share a link please?

comments.author: webdev-dreamer
comments.body: I absolutely despise AI but I have to admit, those one-shots are pretty amazing (given where we were with AI just a few months ago)
